_note: The terms of the Perch levels, in ASD-STE100. Each definition matches the text of the level in content/projects/perch.json. A term shows on the dashboard when the learner passes its level.

terms.definition: A board with many holes. You push parts and wires into the holes. You do not need glue or solder.
A long line at the edge of a breadboard. The red + line is for power. The blue − line is for ground. All the holes on one rail are joined.
A small metal leg on a part. Each pin has one job, and its name tells you the job.
A pin of the ESP32-S3 board. It pushes power out.
Electricity moves in a circle. It goes out of the power pin (+), through a part, and back to the ground pin (−). If the circle is broken, nothing works.
A part that joins two wires only while you press it. Press: the wires touch. Let go: they come apart.
A pin that the board controls. It can listen (is the button pressed?) or talk (turn the light on). GPIO 1 is pin number 1.
A small part that lets less electricity through. Without it, too much goes into the light, and the light burns out.
A small light. It works only one way round. The long leg goes toward power (+), and the short leg goes toward ground (−).
The long leg of an LED. It goes toward power (+).
The short leg of an LED. It goes toward ground (−).
A part that hears sound. This mic turns sound into numbers. It sends the numbers to the board on 3 wires. The wires are a clock wire, a 'which side' wire and a data wire.
A wire that goes on, off, on, off, very fast. Two parts use it to keep the same beat, like two people who clap together.
A part that makes sound louder. The board is too weak to move a speaker. The amp takes the sound from the board and makes it strong enough.
A part that makes sound. It moves in and out very fast, and pushes the air. Your ears hear the moving air as sound.
A small square of 240 × 240 tiny dots. Each dot can be any color. The board tells each dot what color to be, many times each second, and that makes pictures.
